title: Refactor auth adapters and remediate OpenSSL/JWT/SAML compatibility
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months we have accumulated several ad-hoc integrations for SSO/JWT and crypto that expose brittle behavior across services (gateway, auth-bridge, sso-service). Symptoms observed: intermittent SAML assertion validation failures across Java/Python components, token signing/verifying mismatches after OpenSSL ABI changes on build images, and inconsistent JWT claim parsing when different JWT libraries are used in parallel.

Goal: Implement a small, language-agnostic adapter layer and compatibility shims to decouple internal services from direct crypto library behavior. The work includes a targeted OpenSSL bump on build images, harmonizing JWT library usage and parsing expectations, and stabilizing SAML XML canonicalization across our SSO integrations. This must be implemented with comprehensive tests and a canary rollout with observability hooks (trace + failure-rate alerts).
acceptance_criteria: An adapter interface exists and is used by gateway, auth-bridge, and sso-service (compile-time where applicable, mocked for unit tests)
OpenSSL in base build image updated to 3.2.1 (or later stable) with release notes captured and a validated migration checklist
JWT handling unified: dependencies reconciled (jwt-go v4.x for Go services, python-jose v3.2+ for Python) and token tests added that cover edge cases (missing exp, whitespace in claims, alg mismatch)
SAML validations pass for canonical test-suite (existing failing payloads from incidents reproducible and fixed)
End-to-end canary rollout (5% traffic) shows no increase in error-rate, latency, or CPU; metrics captured in dashboard runtime/auth-adapter-canary
Security review completed and sign-off recorded in Confluence and security-scan results attached to the PR
steps: Audit current crypto/JWT/SAML dependencies across services and produce a delta report (scope: gateway, auth-bridge, sso-service)
Design adapter API (Go interface + thin Python/Java wrappers) and publish design doc for review
Implement compatibility shim for legacy token formats and SAML canonicalization differences
Update base images and build pipelines to use OpenSSL 3.2.1; run full integration test matrix in CI
Replace in-repo direct JWT implementation with the chosen library and add property-based tests for claim parsing
Add end-to-end SAML test vectors (from incidents) to CI and validate fixed behavior
Create canary rollout plan, dashboards, and alerts; execute 5% traffic canary and iterate based on metrics
Complete security review, attach findings, and coordinate with platform release to promote to 50% then 100%
notes: Trade-offs: adapter adds a small indirection layer but reduces effort to swap implementations and isolates OpenSSL ABI changes
We will not attempt a full rewrite of SSO service during this ticket — focus is compatibility and stabilization, not feature changes
Some downstream partners use nonstandard SAML payloads; we will add explicit exceptions with audit trails rather than silent normalization
OpenSSL bump requires validating third-party vendor binaries (FFmpeg builds used in analytics) — dependency list included in audit
Introduce a backwards-compatibility flag to enable rollback to old behavior if a critical customer is impacted during rollout
